  Swap has sat at exactly 20 GB for 27 minutes. That's not pressure that's still building — it's pages the crisis pushed out that will stay out until
  the processes owning them exit. My "swap under half" line is a proxy that may never clear on this box, so continuing to wait on it is waiting on the
  wrong number. The metric that actually predicts an OOM is available RAM and whether swap is growing; both are steady.

  I've started nothing, and I'd rather you pick than have me quietly overrule a gate I set an hour ago.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 ☐ How to finish

│ The 260907f work is committed and unpushed, waiting on one clean full-suite run. Three attempts have now been killed or blocked by box conditions
│ rather than by anything in the code. How do you want to close it out?

❯ 1. Run it at low concurrency (Recommended)
     `npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2` in tmux — the neighbourly version. Far less memory than the default fan-out that caused the pile-up, so it can
     run on a box 18 agents share without being the thing that tips it. Slower (maybe 25–40 min rather than 15), but it is a real full-suite pass
     rather than an argument for skipping one.
  2. Push now on existing evidence
     Typecheck clean across all three projects; every file the diff touches green when run individually (changelog-page 32, site-footer 17,
     build-description 8, styles-entry 6, logo-animation 25, plus changelog-file and command-match); the pre-merge run reached 810 passed with all
     three failures explained and fixed. dev builds nothing, so nothing reaches readers — the full suite matters most before `npm run deploy`, which
     is yours to run.
  3. Keep waiting for a quiet box
     Arm another wake-up and try again later, gating on available RAM and load rather than on the stuck swap figure. Safest for the other agents, but
     the work stays unpushed and invisible to the other machine for however long that takes — and the box has not been quiet all night.
  4. Type something.
